name: virtualization_inventory
description: List the VMs, the disk files they name, the snapshots and the datastores that configuration files and inventory exports say exist, from a directory or a list of files. It reads, from their public descriptions and no others: VMware .vmx and .vmsd and ESXi's vmInventory.xml; a libvirt domain XML (devices, disks, backing stores), domain snapshot XML and storage pool XML; a Proxmox VM or container configuration (/etc/pve/qemu-server/<id>.conf, with its snapshot sections; a [special:...] section, such as the cloud-init settings, is listed as special and not as a snapshot) and storage.cfg. A Hyper-V (.vmcx, .vmrs), VirtualBox (.vbox), OVF or VMware template or state file is recognised and listed as unsupported, never guessed at, and a file of no recognised kind is counted by extension. Every record carries its source file id and the line or XML element it came from; versions are the strings the files carry (hardware version, machine type), and what they mean for a release is not stated. A disk a configuration names is looked up only among the files given: `in_set` no is a statement about the set, a hypervisor storage volume is listed and not looked up, and a configuration entry does not show that a VM ran, still exists or was not deleted. A time is derived only where the file states an epoch (Proxmox snaptime, libvirt creationTime, UTC by definition); the two raw fields of a .vmsd are kept raw and not decoded. XML is read with every DOCTYPE and entity declaration refused and the element count and depth bounded; text is read a line at a time with a line cap; a file over max_file_bytes is named and not read; a file with more than 100000 records is partial and says so. An XML file in an encoding the reader does not know fails that file and the run goes on. A Proxmox configuration names its first 200 snapshot and special sections with their totals; every snapshot section is a row of snapshots, paged whole. Every answer carries `status` (complete, partial or failed) and `status_basis`, the pair the recipes' coverage.json carries; exit 0 means the engine ran, not that the examination is complete. SENSITIVE: a configuration can hold a console password, a cloud-init password, an SSH key or a user-data blob under a key this tool does not show: only a fixed list of keys is shown, every other key is counted, and the names (not values) of those that look like credentials are listed with their line, their section and the length of the value, in every section they sit in; a libvirt console password attribute is named to a cap of 200 and counted past it. SENSITIVE: every string the answer shows is judged by the field it fills, in three layers. (1) A name (VM, datastore, snapshot, storage, key), a path or file name, an identifier (GUID, VMFS volume id, naa./eui./t10./wwn- device id, VMware uuid, MAC, CID, number) and a simple value (an enum word, a version, a time) is shown only when it fits the plain grammar of its kind: letters, digits, space and . _ - ( ) + [ ] ' # , & ~ % $ (a path adds / \\ { } and a drive, storage or host:port prefix), no `=` or `@`, a `:` only between digits (or in an id), at most 160 characters for a name (96 for a simple value, 255 for each component of a path), no known token prefix, no secret's name beside a random-looking piece or followed by anything but a word, a tag, a counter, a date or an extension (every word after the name is judged, and groups of 4 characters or more in a row are judged as one), and no run of 16 or more letters and digits that changes class as random text does unless it is a well-formed id, a default Windows machine name or made of words; anything else is `<withheld: N bytes, field F>` (a path component by component; when one is withheld as a piece of a base64 key, the pieces of the key next to it across a `/` are withheld with it, also a piece with something glued to it such as `local:`, `[ds1] ` or a quote; a padded 16- or 20-byte key with a `/` still shows 12 or more characters of itself in at most 0.4% of path fields in the worst position of the slash measured and in 0.04% over all positions; an iqn. or t10. device id is shown as an id, in a field and in free text alike, only when it holds names, not a stretch of random text or of random letters of one case, and a t10. model or serial that holds 2D is plain only in the forms drives write), and its original goes to the values file only with write_text in a job. (2) Every other text (a host name, a description, an annotation, an audit action or actor, a message) is judged on a copy with invisible and formatting characters taken out by Unicode category and the escapes of such characters decoded: user-info up to the last `@`, token-shaped runs, prefixed tokens (ghp_, AKIA, glpat-, sk_live_, SG., AIza and others), a PEM key, a run of more than 18 digits and the value after a name that says it is a secret (password, passwd, passphrase, pwd, secret, token, credential, api, access, account, private, master, shared, signing or encryption key, authorization, bearer, dsn, webhook url, connection string, ssh key, snmp community, pass, pw, auth, sig, sas, otp, psk, pin, with up to two digits after the name; any case, glued or CamelCase, anywhere in the string; and the value of a flag that takes a secret (--password, --passphrase, --secret, --token, --api-key, --access-key, --client-secret, --auth, --authorization, --bearer, --psk, --keypass, --storepass, --userpass, --community, --credential, --pw, --otp, every flag that ends in -key, _key or token or holds secret, such as --secret-key, --master-key, --ssh-key and -key, and every CamelCase one that ends in Key, Token, Password, Pwd, Pass or Secret, such as --apiToken and --adminPassword; also written with one dash, and a key flag in a name also with the value glued to it, --master-keyX; --key-file, --keyboard, -p and -P are not one, and the path of a key file given to a flag that takes a key, such as --key client.key, is shown) and `set password`; a value in angle brackets is a value unless it is a placeholder word such as <redacted> or <password>, and a word after a placeholder is a value too when it is built like a secret: letters and digits with a digit, 8 or more digits, or 8 or more letters of one case that are not a word, some of which, 8 letters of one case, are shown) are withheld, in time linear in the length. (3) The serialised answer, every error answer and every paging-file row are read back and checked by a second check written apart from the first two (its own normaliser, named-secret search and class-transition test); a string it finds suspect is replaced by <withheld: N bytes>, its place and the check are listed in boundary.replaced_at, and the answer is partial. The judging of one run shares max_seconds and a cap of 400 million characters: past either, a string not judged before is withheld by its size, the answer is partial and boundary.stopped_by names the stop. Only the exact names of the files this run made are shown as they are; an extension that is not 1 to 10 letters or digits is counted under (other extensions). A short password used as a name, a token under 16 characters in a name, a value of 4 characters or fewer, a tag, a counter, a date or a time stamp after a secret's name, and the shapes listed with their measured rates in the pack's changelog are not recognised, so run as a job with secret_output: true. write_text: true (refused outside a job) creates $OUT/inventory-values.jsonl, mode 0600, created before anything is read, holding the originals; a file already there is refused by name.

root.description: A directory of the evidence files (a link is refused; links inside it are listed and never followed). Give root, paths, or both

paths.description: Files named one by one (a link or a special file is named and never opened)

limit.description: Rows shown inline per list (default 200); every row is counted and, when there are more, the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in pages.<list>.all_results

max_files.description: The most files taken into the set (default 20000, at most 200000); past it the answer is partial and says where the walk stopped

max_entries.description: The most directory entries listed (default 200000, at most 2000000)

max_depth.description: How deep the walk goes (default 16, at most 64); a deeper directory is named

max_seconds.description: The time to spend (default 50, at most 50); what is left is named and the answer is partial

write_text.description: Write the original of every name or value the answer shows withheld or shortened to one 0600 file under $OUT (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true

max_file_bytes.description: A file over this many bytes is named and not read (default 16777216, at most 268435456); nothing is cut
